**3B.5 Research Note: Bongbong Marcos in 2024**

**Working judgment:** `Mostly narrow/lawful on paper, but with meaningful overreach risk`. I found several genuine governance and transparency safeguards, but also a clear expansion of cyber, military, and security-adjacent capacity with limited visible safeguard architecture. I did not find strong 2024 evidence of Marcos personally using emergency powers or anti-terror tools for collective punishment.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Positive | PBBM approves National Cybersecurity Plan to fortify PH against various threats | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-02-08 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-approves-national-cybersecurity-plan-to-fortify-ph-against-various-threats/ | The plan was presented as policy direction with operational guidelines and was developed with public, private, and academic stakeholders. This is the strongest direct transparency / precaution signal I found. | 3B.5 |
| Positive | PBBM adopts DICT’s National Cybersecurity Plan 2023-2028 | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-04-06 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-adopts-dicts-national-cybersecurity-plan-2023-2028/ | EO 58 made the NCSP a whole-of-nation roadmap and required agencies and LGUs to implement and report on it. That is evidence of institutionalized, not purely ad hoc, security governance. | 3B.5 |
| Positive | The government expanded public access through the eFOI portal and kept a media-literacy / disinformation campaign in place | Philippine News Agency | 2024-01-18 | https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1217036 | Expanding eFOI and maintaining media-literacy/disinformation efforts supports a general transparency posture in digital governance. It is not a full risk-governance regime, but it points toward lawful administration. | 3B.5 |
| Positive | PBBM says Philippines will not use water cannons | Philippine News Agency | 2024-05-06 | https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1224081 | Marcos publicly rejected offensive measures and said the goal was not to raise tensions. This is a direct restraint statement that cuts against reckless or punitive use of force. | 3B.5, 2B.6, 2B.7 |
| Positive | PBBM says PH not in business of instigating wars | Reuters / ThePrint | 2024-06-23 | https://theprint.in/world/philippines-not-in-business-of-instigating-wars-says-president-marcos/2143467/ | Marcos said the military would not resort to force or intimidation and disputes should be settled peacefully. That is a strong general restraint signal, though not a specific legal-oversight reform. | 3B.5, 2B.6, 2B.7 |
| Mixed / Negative | Balikatan 2024 moved toward sensitive islands and added cyber/information-warfare training | Reuters | 2024-03-05 | https://www.yahoo.com/news/philippines-us-hold-military-drills-074919409.html | This shows Marcos tolerated a deterrence-heavy posture that included cyber/information-warfare training near sensitive areas. It does not prove abuse, but it does show expanded coercive capacity. | 3B.5, 2B.8 |
| Mixed / Negative | PBBM signs law for independent, dynamic, future-ready PH defense posture | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-10-08 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-signs-law-for-independent-dynamic-future-ready-ph-defense-posture/ | The defense-posture law expands local defense-tech capacity and names cyber, chemical, radiological, AI, and robotics domains. The record I found does not show matching transparency or safeguard architecture. | 3B.5, 2B.8 |
| Mixed / Negative | Philippines and U.S. hold military drills / maritime drills with allies | Reuters | 2024-03-05 | https://www.yahoo.com/news/philippines-us-hold-military-drills-074919409.html | The drills extended deterrence and operational tempo rather than a narrow internal-security role. That is not abuse by itself, but it is consistent with broader securitization. | 3B.5, 2B.8 |
| Mixed / Negative | United States, Japan, Philippine conduct maritime exercises in South China Sea | Reuters | 2024-12-05 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/united-states-japan-philippine-conduct-maritime-exercises-in-south-china-sea-3758253 | Continued maritime drills after confrontation suggest sustained leverage-building and signaling. This is not proof of intimidation against civilians, but it shows the security posture stayed elevated. | 3B.5, 2B.8 |
| Negative / indirect | Philippines | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines | Red-tagging, libel pressure, blocked sites, and threats against journalists persisted under Marcos. This indicates a coercive information environment that can support administrative control, even if not a direct emergency-powers abuse case. | 3B.5, 3B.3 |
| Negative / indirect | Philippines: Dangerous “Red Tagging” of Labor Leaders | Human Rights Watch | 2024-09-25 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/25/philippines-dangerous-red-tagging-labor-leaders | HRW says officials and police or military members threatened union leaders by linking them to communism. This is strong evidence of tolerated intimidation, though not a clear formal emergency-law abuse. | 3B.5, 3B.3, 3B.2 |
| Negative / indirect | Philippines: “Red-Tagging” Puts Activists at Risk | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/philippines-red-tagging-puts-activists-risk | HRW says red-tagging placed activists at serious risk and was used by officials/supporters to accuse critics of insurgent ties. This undercuts a clean “narrow and lawful” picture. | 3B.5, 3B.3, 3B.2 |

**Synthesis**
- Marcos did put some security governance on a more formal track, especially in cybersecurity and digital governance.
- The strongest lawful-use evidence is the National Cybersecurity Plan, EO 58, and the general restraint statements on force.
- The strongest concern is the broadening of defense-tech and cyber capacity plus a continuing red-tagging environment, which suggests the tools of control remained available and sometimes used coercively by state-linked actors.
- I did not find strong 2024 evidence that Marcos himself used emergency powers or anti-terror laws for overt collective punishment.

**Search gap**
- I did not find a clear 2024 case of Marcos invoking emergency powers in the classic sense.
- I also did not find a definitive example of him personally ordering surveillance or anti-terror measures for mass intimidation, so the negative assessment rests more on enabling environment and securitized policy than on one explicit abusive decree.
